title: AI saves a day a week, then work eats it
hook: POV: AI GAVE YOU YOUR FRIDAY BACK

lines: Okay, picture this. AI hands you back almost one whole day, every week.
That's not a dream. About three thousand professionals said AI saves them nineteen percent of their week.
And most of them use it. Seventy-four percent, at work. Not a few nerds. Most of us.
So where did all that free time go? Naps? Long lunches? Nope.
But here's the twist. Seventy-two percent of that time... went straight back into work.
Half of them took on new projects. More tasks. More responsibility. The free day? Gone.
And there's pressure too. Nearly half of workers fear being judged... for not using AI enough.
Forty-eight percent fear being judged for using it too little.
Only twenty percent fear being judged for using it.
Small note. This is what people say about their own work, not measured output.
So here's my question. Did AI give you your time back... or just more to do?
Tomorrow, why some people save far more. Tell me in the comments.

meta.topic: A London School of Economics and Protiviti survey of 3001 professionals: AI saves 19 percent of the working week, most of it reinvested in more work, and 48 percent fear being judged for not using AI enough
meta.next_question: Why do trained workers save more time with AI than untrained ones?

facts.claim: A survey of 3,001 professionals found 74 percent use AI at work
Respondents said AI saves them an average of 19 percent of their working week, and they reinvested 72 percent of that time in other work
Half said they use the saved time to take on new responsibilities or projects
48 percent worry about being judged for not using AI enough versus 20 percent worried about being judged for using it
The findings are self-reported perceptions, not independently measured productivity
